A padded TLS session, smoothing the TLS-in-TLS shape other TLS transports leak.
Tries each disguise in turn and remembers what worked on this network.
TLS aimed at a decoy site, so the traffic looks like an ordinary visit there.
UDP and QUIC instead of TCP. Worth a try when every TCP connection dies.
Borrows a real site\'s TLS handshake, so probes see a genuine site. The strongest disguise.
Regions that don\'t offer the selected method are hidden from the region list.
No TLS at all, so a block aimed at TLS misses it.
Connection method updated. Reconnect for it to take effect.
Still working on it. We\'ll try other servers if needed.

PangeaVPN is built to know as little about you as possible. This is everything the service keeps, and why.

Your account number, stored encrypted. For each device, its public key, tunnel address and the name you give it, so our servers can accept its connection. Your plan\'s dates, plus Apple\'s transaction ID if you subscribe in the app, so we know your plan is active.

Your account number, stored encrypted. For each device, its public key, tunnel address and the name you give it, so our servers can accept its connection. Your plan\'s dates, so we know your plan is active.
The sites you visit, your traffic, your DNS lookups, when you connect or disconnect, and your IP address.
Sent only when you tap Send Report. Account numbers, keys and IP addresses are stripped on your device first, and reports are deleted after 30 days.
Nothing about your use of the VPN is ever sold, used for anything but running PangeaVPN, or shared with anyone.
Copies the app version, connection status, settings and recent logs. Your account number is never included.
Debugging diagnostics. Leave these off unless you were asked to turn one on.
The tunnel log is available while the VPN is on.

Devices signed in to your account.

Time added — you can connect again.
Traffic is held inside the VPN while it reconnects or switches servers.
If iOS stops the VPN, it restarts itself when Auto-connect is on.
All traffic is routed into the VPN, and IPv6 is blocked so it can\'t leak.
Lockdown, under Startup, keeps the VPN on from inside PangeaVPN and hides the Disconnect button.
With Auto-connect on, PangeaVPN reconnects after drops and after your device restarts.
Their current state shows here while PangeaVPN is connected.

Android itself can block every connection outside PangeaVPN, even when the VPN is off. To turn this on, open VPN settings, tap the gear next to PangeaVPN, then turn on Always-on VPN and Block connections without VPN.
CarPlay and Personal Hotspot may not work.
AirDrop, AirPlay and printing need Allow LAN.
Some Apple system services may still bypass the VPN.
Updating PangeaVPN while connected can leave your device offline until it restarts.
How PangeaVPN keeps your traffic from leaking outside the VPN.
Sends every connection through the VPN, including ones iOS would otherwise let out. Applies on next connect.
Strict kill switch off. Applies on next connect.
Strict kill switch on. Applies on next connect.
Only VPN traffic is allowed until you reconnect or turn off the kill switch.
iOS sets the language for each app. In the page that opens, tap Language and pick one. If Language isn\'t there, first add the language in General › Language & Region.
Couldn\'t open Settings. Open the Settings app and choose PangeaVPN.
This account already has the maximum number of devices. Remove one to continue.

We don\'t recognise that account number. Check it and try again.
Too many sign-in attempts. Wait a minute, then try again.

Our servers are having trouble. Please try again in a moment.
Signing in took too long. Check your connection and try again.
Sign in failed. Please try again.
Couldn\'t reach PangeaVPN. Check your internet connection and try again.
Your account number is in Settings in any PangeaVPN app you\'re signed in to, and on your account page on the PangeaVPN website.
Find your account number at pangeavpn.org/account
Turn it off in Settings to disconnect.
Internet is paused until the VPN is back.
Allow LAN disabled. Reconnect for it to take effect.
Allow LAN enabled. Reconnect for it to take effect.
DNS restored to the VPN default. Takes effect on next connect.
Pick a resolver, or enter your own. Filtering comes from that service. Applies on next connect.
DNS set to %1$s. Takes effect on next connect.
Enter a whole number between %1$d and %2$d.
Tunnel MTU set to %1$d. Takes effect on next connect.
Adds a quantum-resistant key to the tunnel, so traffic recorded today can\'t be decrypted later. Applies on next connect.
Post-quantum key disabled. Reconnect for it to take effect.
Post-quantum key enabled. Reconnect for it to take effect.
Tells you when the VPN drops, comes back, or is blocking traffic.
Notifications for PangeaVPN are turned off, so alerts can\'t be shown.
Couldn\'t open Settings. Allow notifications for PangeaVPN in your device\'s Settings app.
Notifications for PangeaVPN are off in iOS Settings, so alerts can\'t be shown.
PangeaVPN needs your permission to show alerts.
This disconnects, erases all PangeaVPN data and the VPN profile from this device, and returns to sign-in. It can\'t be undone.
A quick way to erase PangeaVPN from this device and restore your network.

Adds a “Wipe data” action to the PangeaVPN icon\'s long-press menu. Choosing it disconnects, erases all PangeaVPN data and the VPN profile from this device, and returns to sign-in. Delete the app afterwards to remove it entirely. This can\'t be undone.
Runs the same wipe straight away, whether or not panic wipe is on.
If the methods above run out of addresses, the app can fetch replacements from a signed public file.
Address recovery on — used only when every method above has failed.
It\'s off because it shows our domain to anyone watching your network. Testing it does the same, once.
No address stored yet, and encrypted DNS is off
Enter through one server, leave through another. The network you\'re on only ever sees the entry.
No entry server is available right now
You\'re still signed in on this device, but PangeaVPN couldn\'t reach its servers. Check your connection, then try again.
Sign in with your account number to rename devices.
Failed to rename device. Please try again.
Use 1 to 40 characters for the name.

Confirm it\'s you to see your account number.

Fetches a signed address list from a public host, checked on your device. Last resort, and it carries no account details.
Ways to fetch your VPN profile, tried in the order listed. Keep at least one on.
Connects by IP, no DNS lookup.
Goes through a relay on a large content network, at an address too widely shared to block cheaply. The relay can\'t read what it passes on.
At least one connection method must stay on.
Plain HTTPS and a normal DNS lookup. Tried last: it\'s the only one that exposes our domain.
Tunnels account traffic through REALITY, which looks like a visit to an ordinary website.
Tunnels account traffic through Shadowsocks, so nobody sees which server you reach.

This permanently deletes your PangeaVPN account, its remaining time and every device on it. It can\'t be undone. Deleting doesn\'t cancel an Apple subscription: cancel that separately in your Apple ID settings.
This permanently deletes your PangeaVPN account, its remaining time and every device on it. It can\'t be undone.
Couldn\'t delete your account. Check your connection and try again.
The VPN disconnects and this device leaves your account. You\'ll need your account number to sign in again.
Block all traffic outside the tunnel. Takes effect on the next connect.
Lets local traffic (router, printers, captive portals) skip the tunnel. Turn it on if Wi-Fi keeps dropping to \"No internet\". Applies on next connect.
Tunnel settings and fixes for restrictive Wi-Fi.
IPv4 addresses, comma-separated. Blank uses the VPN default. Applies on next connect.
Enter one or more valid IPv4 DNS addresses separated by commas.
Packet size through the tunnel. Lower it if pages hang on a network that otherwise works. Default 1380. Applies on next connect.
Split tunnelling is off, so these apps still use the VPN.
Addresses listed here bypass the VPN and use your normal connection.
Off sends everything through the VPN. Your ranges are kept. Applies on next connect.
Off sends everything through the VPN. Your apps and ranges are kept. Applies on next connect.
Not an IPv4 address or range: %1$s.
Too many ranges. Remove some first.
Apps switched on here bypass the VPN and use your normal connection.
Individual apps can\'t be left out: iOS only lets a VPN exclude address ranges.
Name lookups (DNS) still go through the VPN.
For devices on your own network, turn on Allow LAN instead.
Changes apply on next connect. Restart an app that was already open.
Strict kill switch is on, so iOS sends everything through the VPN and these ranges are ignored.
Apps and addresses you exclude here bypass the VPN and use your normal connection.
IPv4 addresses or ranges, separated by commas. Applies on next connect.
Split tunnelling off. Applies on next connect.
Split tunnelling on. Applies on next connect.

While it\'s on, PangeaVPN connects again after your device restarts, as long as it still has permission to run a VPN. Turning the VPN off in system settings stops it until you connect in PangeaVPN again.
Connects when your device starts or the network returns, and reconnects if the tunnel drops. Disconnecting in PangeaVPN pauses it until you connect again.
While it\'s on, iOS may turn the VPN back on if you switch it off in Control Center or iOS Settings. To stop it, disconnect in PangeaVPN.
Keeps the VPN on at all times. The Disconnect button is hidden until you turn Lockdown off.
Auto-connect on. PangeaVPN reconnects after drops and when the network returns.
Lockdown off. You can disconnect again.
Lockdown on. The VPN stays on until you turn Lockdown off.
Your plan is already active, so there\'s nothing to buy here. You can subscribe in the app once it ends.

Change or cancel your plan in your Apple ID settings.
Change or cancel your plan on the PangeaVPN website.
Your plan, how it\'s billed, and App Store purchases.
Restore Purchases adds an App Store subscription on this Apple ID to this account.
Send your logs to support with personal details stripped out. You get a code to quote in your email.
The report did not reach us. Check your internet connection and try again.
No mail app is set up. Write to %1$s instead.
The server refused the report. Wait a minute and try again.
The report is anonymous. We cannot tell who sent it, so you will get a short code to quote in your email.
This sends your app log and the VPN service log to support. Account numbers and keys are stripped out first, and so is your IP address.
Quote this code in your email to support.

PangeaVPN updates through the App Store. Turn on automatic updates in Settings › App Store.
